pre_mortem: If Jones loses, the likely mistaken assumption is that his recent workload persists: an unreported restriction, redistribution of carries or an Indianapolis lead could remove rushing volume, and his 72 receiving yards across three games may not compensate. Indianapolis's 5.01 YPC allowed also need not translate to Jones's individual efficiency. If Hockenson loses, the central weakness is treating a defensive location split as a player-specific opportunity without route charting; Minnesota could attack elsewhere or stop throwing after taking a lead. His 137 yards across three games do not reveal whether production was concentrated in one outing. The Jones read is better supported; Hockenson remains a lean rather than a core anchor.
